recs.title: Revisiting Character-Based Neural Machine Translation with Capacity and Compression
recs.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
recs.summary: The modeling problem can be solved by standard sequence-to-sequence architectures of sufficient depth, and that deep models operating at the character level outperform identical models operating over word fragments, implying that alternative architectures for handling character input are better viewed as methods for reducing computation time than as improved ways of modeling longer sequences.

recs.title: Mining Numbers in Text: A Survey
recs.summary: A quick overview of the history and recent advances of the research of mining such relations between numerals and words found in text data is provided.

recs.title: Character-Aware Neural Language Models
recs.summary: A simple neural language model that relies only on character-level inputs that is able to encode, from characters only, both semantic and orthographic information and suggests that on many languages, character inputs are sufficient for language modeling.

recs.title: Exploring the Limits of Language Modeling
recs.summary: This work explores recent advances in Recurrent Neural Networks for large scale Language Modeling, and extends current models to deal with two key challenges present in this task: corpora and vocabulary sizes, and complex, long term structure of language.

recs.title: Byte Pair Encoding is Suboptimal for Language Model Pretraining
recs.summary: Differences between BPE and unigram LM tokenization are analyzed, finding that the latter method recovers subword units that align more closely with morphology and avoids problems stemming from BPE’s greedy construction procedure.

recs.title: SuperBPE: Space Travel for Language Models
recs.summary: A "superword"tokenizer, SuperBPE, is introduced, which incorporates a simple pretokenization curriculum into the byte-pair encoding (BPE) algorithm to first learn subwords, then superwords that bridge whitespace, resulting in segmentations of text that are more uniform in per-token difficulty.

recs.title: Proxy Compression for Language Modeling
recs.summary: This work introduces proxy compression, an alternative training scheme that preserves the efficiency benefits of compressed inputs while providing an end-to-end, raw-byte interface at inference time, and substantially improves training efficiency and significantly outperforms pure byte-level baselines given fixed compute budgets.

recs.title: Systematic review and comparative synthesis of cross lingual question answering systems for low resource Indic languages
recs.summary: A systematic review of 137 shortlisted research articles reveals that the performance of a cross-lingual QA system is structurally influenced by the interaction between linguistic typology, model design, and not exclusively by model scale or architecture.

recs.title: Scratchpad Patching: Decoupling Compute from Patch Size in Byte-Level Language Models
recs.summary: This work introduces Scratchpad Patching (SP), which inserts transient scratchpads inside each patch to aggregate the bytes seen so far and refresh patch-level context for subsequent predictions, and improves model quality at the same patch size.

recs.title: Learning to Automatically Solve Algebra Word Problems
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: An approach for automatically learning to solve algebra word problems by reasons across sentence boundaries to construct and solve a system of linear equations, while simultaneously recovering an alignment of the variables and numbers to the problem text.

recs.title: CharBERT: Character-aware Pre-trained Language Model
recs.summary: This paper proposes a character-aware pre-trained language model named CharBERT improving on the previous methods (such as BERT, RoBERTa) and proposes a new pre-training task named NLM (Noisy LM) for unsupervised character representation learning.

recs.title: Fully Character-Level Neural Machine Translation without Explicit Segmentation
recs.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: A neural machine translation model that maps a source character sequence to a target character sequence without any segmentation is introduced, allowing the model to be trained at a speed comparable to subword-level models while capturing local regularities.

recs.title: Retrofitting (Large) Language Models with Dynamic Tokenization
recs.summary: This work proposes retrofitting LMs with dynamic tokenization: a way to dynamically decide on token boundaries based on the input text via a subword-merging algorithm inspired by byte-pair encoding that can mitigate the limitations of static tokenization.

recs.title: Injecting the score of the first-stage retriever as text improves BERT-based re-rankers
recs.summary: A novel approach for combining first-stage lexical retrieval models and Transformer-based re-rankers is proposed, which injects the relevance score of the lexical model as a token into the input of the cross-encoder re-ranker.

recs.title: Sampling from Your Language Model One Byte at a Time
recs.summary: An inference-time method to convert any autoregressive LM with a BPE tokenizer into a character-level or byte-level LM and is also able to unify the vocabularies of language models with different tokenizers, allowing one to ensemble LMs with different tokenizers at inference time or transfer the post-training from one model to another using proxy-tuning.

recs.title: Bolmo: Byteifying the Next Generation of Language Models
recs.summary: Bolmo is introduced, a family of fully open byte-level LLMs that approach the capabilities of subword-based systems, demonstrating that models operating on raw text encodings can scale competitively while offering advantages in domains requiring fine-grained textual understanding.

recs.title: Improving Multilingual Models with Language-Clustered Vocabularies
recs.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
recs.summary: This work introduces a novel procedure for multilingual vocabulary generation that combines the separately trained vocabularies of several automatically derived language clusters, thus balancing the trade-off between cross-lingual subword sharing and language-specific vocABularies.

recs.title: Achieving Open Vocabulary Neural Machine Translation with Hybrid Word-Character Models
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: A novel word-character solution to achieving open vocabulary NMT that can successfully learn to not only generate well-formed words for Czech, a highly-inflected language with a very complex vocabulary, but also build correct representations for English source words.

recs.title: Why don’t people use character-level machine translation?
recs.summary: It is shown that even with recent modeling innovations in character-level natural language processing, character- level MT systems still struggle to match their subword-based counterparts, and show neither better domain robustness, nor better morphological generalization.

recs.title: An Empirical Investigation of Contextualized Number Prediction
recs.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
recs.summary: A suite of output distribution parameterizations are introduced that incorporate latent variables to add expressivity and better fit the natural distribution of numeric values in running text, and combine them with both recur-rent and transformer-based encoder architectures.

recs.title: MAGNET: Improving the Multilingual Fairness of Language Models with Adaptive Gradient-Based Tokenization
Beyond Text Compression: Evaluating Tokenizers Across Scales
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: It is shown that smaller models can accurately predict significant differences in tokenizer impact on larger models at a fraction of the compute cost, and proposes new intrinsic tokenizer metrics inspired by Zipf's law that correlate more strongly with downstream performance than text compression when modeling unseen languages.

recs.title: MoCE: Adaptive Mixture of Contextualization Experts for Byte-based Neural Machine Translation
recs.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: This work proposes Mixture of Contextualization Experts (MoCE), adaptively selecting and mixing attention heads, which are treated as contextualization experts, which enhances the flexibility of contextualization scales and allows models to search for better contextualization combinations.

recs.title: NUMCoT: Numerals and Units of Measurement in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning using Large Language Models
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: This paper anatomizes the reasoning of math word problems to different sub-procedures like numeral conversions from language to numbers and measurement conversions based on units and demonstrates that LLMs still encounter difficulties in handling numeral and measurement conversions.

recs.title: Rate-Utility Frontiers for Language Encodings: Comparing Tokens, Bytes, and Pixels Under Controlled Linguistic Content
recs.summary: This work uses verified parallel sentences to compare tokens, bytes, and pixels through a shared bottleneck whose width is swept to trace rate-utility frontiers, and evaluates three utilities: surface form preservation, cross-lingual sentence alignment, and topic classification.
